planner_model: dynamic-programming cost-based planner with GEQO fallback
stats_and_costing: rich per-rel/path costing, selectivity, pathkeys, bitmap costing
index_model: btree, hash, GiST, SP-GiST, GIN, BRIN, bitmap, index-only
transaction_or_visibility_model: MVCC with heap visibility, proc array, clog, visibility map
strongest_differentiators: planner completeness and exact/recheck-aware AM contract
highest_value_borrow_points: canonical planner front door, mature path/property model, exact-vs-lossy AM contract, visibility map/index-only discipline
main_current_limit: less family-specialized than some newer engines and still centered on heap recheck for many AMs

planner_model: cost-based stream/rivers optimizer tied tightly to retrieval and MGA semantics
stats_and_costing: selectivity and cardinality driven stream ordering, index-driven navigation, unique-index short-circuit
index_model: compressed B-tree with jump nodes, compound matching, navigation, inversion composition
transaction_or_visibility_model: native MGA with savepoints, snapshots, VIO-owned version chase/backout
highest_value_borrow_points: single semantic owner for visibility/backout, index use inside MGA-native record lifecycle
main_current_limit: narrower AM family breadth than PostgreSQL-class systems

planner_model: hypergraph join optimizer layered over classic optimizer and range subsystem
stats_and_costing: interesting orders, hypergraph cost model, range estimates, ICP/MRR-aware costing
index_model: clustered InnoDB PK, secondary B-trees, ref/range/index merge/skip scans, ICP, MRR
transaction_or_visibility_model: InnoDB consistent-read via read views, undo/version chain, purge
strongest_differentiators: broad access-path menu and strong interesting-order handling
highest_value_borrow_points: hypergraph join search, interesting order framework, ICP/MRR, clustered/secondary split discipline
main_current_limit: still split between newer hypergraph front end and older optimizer subsystems

planner_model: classic cost/range optimizer with strong range/index_merge machinery and engine-specific delegation
stats_and_costing: SEL_TREE interval analysis, partition pruning, filesort and min-max shortcuts
index_model: InnoDB B-tree baseline plus engine/plugin-specific alternatives
transaction_or_visibility_model: InnoDB visibility for transactional engines, plugin-specific behaviors elsewhere
strongest_differentiators: very mature range and partition pruning machinery
highest_value_borrow_points: range tree formalism, group-by-minmax, partition pruning, storage-engine contract separation
main_current_limit: less unified than MySQL hypergraph path and highly dependent on chosen storage engine

planner_model: logical-plan optimizer with query graph join ordering and vectorized execution coherence
stats_and_costing: statistics propagation, join-order cost model, row-group pruning, late materialization
index_model: storage statistics, row-group pruning, ART/storage index use where available
transaction_or_visibility_model: single-node transactional engine but major win is vectorized scan/prune coherence
highest_value_borrow_points: row-group pruning, late materialization, stats propagation, vectorized-aware planning
main_current_limit: index family breadth is intentionally smaller than general-purpose SQL engines

planner_model: query-tree planner plus storage-driven pruning and pipeline planning
stats_and_costing: primary-key and skip-index condition evaluation, projection and read-algorithm selection
index_model: MergeTree sparse primary key, partition pruning, minmax/set/bloom/text/vector skip indexes, projections
transaction_or_visibility_model: part-level atomicity and refresh/publication, not row-MVCC
highest_value_borrow_points: primary-key condition interpreter, skip index framework, projections, approximate vector within storage
main_current_limit: not a fully general row-MVCC optimizer and many indices are pruning aids rather than exact tuple locators

planner_model: read-path and index-plan selection, not full relational cost-based optimization
stats_and_costing: index plan selection is driven by query form, token range, repair strictness, and SSTable coverage
index_model: LSM/SSTable-attached indexes, SAI, SASI, memtable + SSTable query views
highest_value_borrow_points: segment/SSTable-attached index publication, strict vs non-strict filtering, memtable+disk merge semantics
main_current_limit: no broad cost-based relational join/order optimizer

planner_model: query canonicalization plus index tagging, plan enumeration, multiplanning and cost-based ranking
stats_and_costing: heuristic rewrites, memo enumeration, plan cache, cost-based ranker, SBE lowering
index_model: B-tree, multikey, sparse, partial, wildcard, text, geo, clustered scan, index intersection
transaction_or_visibility_model: storage snapshot consistency and multikey/index metadata semantics
strongest_differentiators: plan enumeration plus runtime plan competition
highest_value_borrow_points: index-tagging pipeline, memo plan enumeration, multikey/wildcard handling, plan cache discipline
main_current_limit: still split between classic query planner, multiplanner, and newer cost-based/SBE layers

planner_model: per-shard query rewrite and collector planning over Lucene
stats_and_costing: rewrite pipeline, collector selection, index-sort early termination, aggregation rewrites
index_model: inverted index, postings, doc values, BKD/point trees, star-tree, vector and completion families
transaction_or_visibility_model: near-real-time refresh and PIT/search contexts, not MGA MVCC
highest_value_borrow_points: query rewrite pipeline, index-sort early termination, collector specialization, per-family query builders
main_current_limit: not a relational cost-based optimizer with join search

stats_and_costing: no generic planner; each command owns its own algorithm
index_model: native data structures, sorted-set/geohash for GEO, modules for custom indexes
transaction_or_visibility_model: single-threaded command serialization with MULTI/EXEC, not MVCC
highest_value_borrow_points: hard specialization, partial sort, encoded-score search, module extension boundary
main_current_limit: no general optimizer or native multi-index plan search in core server

planner_model: cost-based Cypher logical planner with graph statistics and IDP-style connectors
stats_and_costing: statistics-backed cardinality, interesting orders, graph-pattern costing
index_model: range/text/fulltext/vector families routed through node/relationship index seek/scan runtimes and GB+Tree-backed schema indexes
transaction_or_visibility_model: transaction-state-aware graph indexes and uniqueness/locking semantics
highest_value_borrow_points: interesting-order graph planning, nested index joins, node/relationship specific seek operators, tx-state index visibility
main_current_limit: planner is graph-centric rather than broad relational-family

planner_model: plan parsing plus coordinator-driven ANN/scalar execution routing
stats_and_costing: segment state, coordinator routing, top-k merging, search-iterator tuning
index_model: per-segment ANN indexes, scalar filters, text/tantivy bindings, offset-mapped vector search
transaction_or_visibility_model: timestamp/segment visibility with guarantee-ts, not MGA MVCC
highest_value_borrow_points: asynchronous index build/publication, sealed vs growing segment routing, vector+bitset execution discipline
main_current_limit: not a general SQL cost-based optimizer and exact relational semantics are secondary

planner_model: delegation to DataFusion/IOx planner with time-series rewrite layers
stats_and_costing: chunk statistics, chunk filters, query rewrites, cache-assisted chunk selection
index_model: table/chunk indexes over parquet and buffered data, time/series pruning, cache-backed metadata
transaction_or_visibility_model: snapshot and persisted-file sequencing, not row-MVCC
strongest_differentiators: time-series chunk pruning and cache integration
highest_value_borrow_points: chunk filter derivation, buffer+parquet union planning, metadata-driven pruning
main_current_limit: index semantics are metadata and chunk oriented, not broad secondary-access-method planning
